title: Best Travel Insurance Providers of 2026
intro_mdx_or_text: Travel insurance is one of the hardest products to comparison-shop: every premium is quote-based — varying by trip cost, traveler age, dates, and your state — and the benefit that matters most is buried in policy wording. This guide compares five major US providers for 2026: Allianz Travel Insurance, Travel Guard (AIG), Seven Corners, World Nomads, and Travelex. Because prices are quote-based, we deliberately compare published plan structure instead of inventing representative premiums: single-trip and annual lineups, Cancel For Any Reason terms and their conditions, free-look periods, named underwriters, and documented assistance services, each cited to the provider's official pages as of 2026-07-18. Important honesty notes: Vivahale is not an insurance agency or broker and does not sell policies; we have not filed claims with these providers and do not survey their customers — our ratings analyze each insurer's own published documentation. Benefits and availability vary by state (several plans here cannot be sold in New York or Washington at all), so verify your state's terms in the official plan documents. We score each provider on five weighted criteria: Value (30%), Experience (25%), Flexibility (20%), Transparency (15%), and Service (10%). Affiliate compensation never affects ranking or scores.
answer_block: For most travelers in 2026, Allianz is our top pick on published terms: its Cancel Anytime upgrade states the highest reimbursement in this comparison — 80% of lost non-refundable trip costs, cancellable through the day of departure — alongside four single-trip and four annual plans (as of 2026-07-18). Travel Guard is best for customization, with documented add-on bundles from adventure sports to pet and wedding coverage, though its CFAR reimburses "typically 50%". Seven Corners offers 75% CFAR on both mid-market plans plus the group's only Interruption For Any Reason option. World Nomads is best for adventurers: 250–340+ documented activities and the unique ability to buy or extend coverage mid-trip. Travelex has the longest free look at 21 days. All pricing is quote-based; benefits vary by state. We weight Value 30%, Experience 25%, Flexibility 20%, Transparency 15%, and Service 10% — Vivahale analyzes published documentation, not claims experience.

faq.question: Which travel insurance company is best in 2026?
faq.answer: On published documentation there is no single winner for everyone. We rank Allianz first for the strongest Cancel For Any Reason-style terms (80% via Cancel Anytime); Travel Guard for documented add-on customization; Seven Corners for 75% CFAR access on mid-priced plans plus IFAR; World Nomads for adventure activities and buying coverage mid-trip; and Travelex for the longest free look (21 days). All facts cited to official provider pages as of 2026-07-18; benefits vary by state.

faq.question: Why don't you show prices for these plans?
faq.answer: Because none exist to show honestly: every provider here prices by quote, varying with trip cost, traveler age, dates, and state, and none publishes a fixed list price (as of 2026-07-18). Rather than invent a 'representative' premium, we compare what is actually published — plan structures, CFAR terms, free-look periods, and underwriters — and link you to the official quote flows.

faq.question: What is Cancel For Any Reason (CFAR) coverage?
faq.answer: CFAR is an optional upgrade that partially reimburses your nonrefundable trip costs when you cancel for a reason your base policy doesn't cover. Published terms in this comparison range from "typically 50%" (Travel Guard) to 75% (Seven Corners, Travelex, World Nomads' Epic) to 80% (Allianz's Cancel Anytime). Every provider attaches conditions — purchase windows measured from your first trip payment, cancellation deadlines before departure, and state restrictions (it is commonly unavailable in New York) — so read the exact conditions in your plan documents.

faq.question: Do you actually test these insurers or file claims?
faq.answer: No. Vivahale is not an insurance agency or broker, has not filed claims with these providers, and does not survey policyholders. Our ratings analyze each insurer's own published documentation — plan pages, policy wording, free-look and CFAR terms, and named underwriters — cited with as-of dates. Treat this guide as a structured reading of the official record, then verify your state's terms before buying.

faq.question: How do we rank these providers?
faq.answer: We use a fixed, published methodology weighting Value (30%), Experience (25%), Flexibility (20%), Transparency (15%), and Service (10%). Facts come only from each provider's official pages, every changeable figure carries an as-of date, and affiliate relationships never affect scores or order — our #2 pick, Travel Guard, earns us nothing.

title: Best Carry-On Luggage of 2026
intro_mdx_or_text: Carry-on suitcases are one of the few travel purchases where the facts you need are actually published: exact dimensions, weight, capacity, materials, and — most tellingly — what the warranty really covers. This guide compares four widely used carry-ons for 2026: the Travelpro Platinum Elite 21″ Expandable Spinner, the Briggs & Riley Baseline Essential Carry-On Expandable Spinner, Away's The Carry-On, and the Monos Carry-On. Every price is the US list price from the brand's official site as of 2026-07-18 (prices change and sales are frequent, so verify before buying), and every dimension, weight, and warranty claim is cited to official brand documentation. An honesty note: Vivahale does not lab-test luggage, run drop tests, or survey owners — we read and compare what each brand publishes, which is why warranty wording and published specs weigh heavily here. We initially scoped a fifth widely sold bag (Samsonite's Freeform Carry-On) but excluded it because we could not verify its full specifications from official pages at review time — we do not fill gaps with guesses. We score each bag on five weighted criteria: Value (30%), Experience (25%), Flexibility (20%), Transparency (15%), and Service (10%). Affiliate compensation never affects ranking or scores.
answer_block: For most frequent flyers in 2026, the Travelpro Platinum Elite 21″ is our top pick on published terms: the largest documented capacity here (46 L, expandable), airline-damage coverage via its Trusted Companion Promise, and the only 100-day trial that refunds a used bag — at $390 list (as of 2026-07-18). The Briggs & Riley Baseline Essential ($695) is the buy-it-for-life pick, with the only unconditional lifetime guarantee — airline damage included, no proof of purchase. Away's The Carry-On ($275) is the best all-rounder per dollar: 41 L polycarbonate hardware plus the clearly documented LifetimeCare™ repair program. The Monos Carry-On ($275) is the lightest verified bag (7.01 lb) and the only one matching the big airlines' published 22 x 14 x 9 in. limit exactly. We weight Value 30%, Experience 25%, Flexibility 20%, Transparency 15%, Service 10% — ratings analyze published documentation, not lab testing.

faq.question: Which carry-on suitcase is best in 2026?
faq.answer: On published documentation: the Travelpro Platinum Elite 21″ for overall capacity and the most generous documented trial-and-warranty package at $390; the Briggs & Riley Baseline Essential for its unconditional lifetime guarantee at $695; Away's The Carry-On as the best-documented all-rounder at $275; and the Monos Carry-On for the lightest verified weight and exact airline-limit dimensions, also $275. All prices are US list from official brand pages as of 2026-07-18.

faq.question: What size carry-on do US airlines actually allow?
faq.answer: American, Delta, and United each publish a 22 x 14 x 9 in. maximum including wheels and handles. Of the bags here, only the Monos Carry-On's published exterior matches that limit exactly; Away's is 0.4 in. over on width, and Travelpro's exterior-with-wheels measurement (23 x 14.5 x 9 in.) relies on its 21 x 14 x 9 in. case dimension to fit. Always check your specific airline's published limits — smaller regional and international carriers can be stricter.

faq.question: Which luggage warranty is actually the best?
faq.answer: Read the wording, not the headline. Briggs & Riley's "Simple as that®" guarantee is the only unconditional one here — any damage, even by an airline, repaired free for life, no proof of purchase. Travelpro pairs a lifetime limited warranty on named components with airline-damage coverage via its Trusted Companion Promise. Away's LifetimeCare™ gives five years of complimentary repairs, then lifetime repair support. Monos advertises a lifetime warranty but publishes the least detail about what it covers (all as of 2026-07-18).

faq.question: Do you actually test these suitcases?
faq.answer: No — and we say so on every review. Vivahale does not lab-test, drop-test, or survey owners. We compare what each brand officially publishes: list price, dimensions, weight, capacity, materials, warranty wording, and trial terms, each cited with an as-of date. Where a brand doesn't publish a fact (as with Samsonite's Freeform at review time), we exclude rather than guess.

faq.question: How do we rank these bags?
faq.answer: We use a fixed, published methodology weighting Value (30%), Experience (25%), Flexibility (20%), Transparency (15%), and Service (10%). Facts come only from official brand documentation, every price carries an as-of date, and affiliate relationships never affect scores or order — our #2 pick, Briggs & Riley, earns us nothing.
